defects.description: French 15-year-olds' life expectancy is said to rise from 58 to 83, 'an increase of 35 years', but 83 - 58 = 25 years.
paraphrases: 83 minus 58 is 25, not the stated 35-year increase.
The rise from 58 to 83 years is miscalculated as 35.
The stated increase does not match the two figures given (it should be 25).
defects.rationale: Correct value '25 years' (83 - 58). Findable from the two figures in the same sentence, distinct.

defects.description: Life expectancy is said to have 'more than doubled' from 32 to 61 years, but 32 doubled is 64, so 61 is less than double, not more.
paraphrases: 32 more than doubled would exceed 64, but 61 is below that, so it did not more than double.
'More than doubled to 61' contradicts the starting value of 32 (2 x 32 = 64 > 61).
The claim of more-than-doubling is inconsistent with the 32-to-61 change.
defects.rationale: Correct value '71 years' (> 2 x 32). Findable from the 32 figure and the doubling claim in the same passage, distinct.

defects.description: Global 2021 life expectancy (just over 70) is said to be 'more than twice' the value two centuries earlier, given as 'less than 45'; but twice 45 is 90, which exceeds 70, so 70 is not more than twice 45.
paraphrases: If the earlier value was under 45, more than twice it would exceed 90, but 2021 is only about 70.
'More than twice ... less than 45' is inconsistent with a 2021 value of just over 70.
70 cannot be more than double a figure as high as 45 (that would require over 90).
defects.rationale: Correct value 'less than 35 years' (half of ~70). Findable from the ~70 figure and the 'more than twice' claim in the same sentence, distinct.
